drhp.business: The growing industrial utilization of precious metals, particularly silver and platinum group metals, is adding a significant structural demand dimension beyond traditional consumption patterns. Silver's superior electrical and thermal conductivity makes it indispensable in solar photovoltaic cell manufacturing, electronics, EV components, and emerging data center infrastructure. As India accelerates its renewable energy ambitions, the demand for silver in solar panel production has intensified substantially.

risks: We intend to utilise a portion of the Net Proceeds towards the acquisition and installation of plant and machinery for the proposed expansion of our manufacturing facility.

Our Company proposes to utilise ₹285.00 lakhs out of the Net Proceeds of the Issue towards the purchase and installation of additional machinery for the proposed expansion of its manufacturing facility.

Our Company has identified certain plant and machinery proposed to be acquired and installed at its manufacturing facility situated at Gala No. 10, Building No. 3, Jay Chamundeshwari Industrial Complex, Valiv, Vasai East, Maharashtra, India.
The proposed expenditure is based on quotations obtained from Marshal Manufacture and Yadgaar Enterprises.
We have obtained quotations from respective vendors / suppliers and is yet to place any orders or enter into definitive agreements for purchase of plant & machinery.
Accordingly, we cannot assure you that the proposed plant and machinery will be procured at the estimated cost or within the anticipated timelines.
While we may seek to mitigate the impact of unforeseen events, there can be no assurance that all delays, disruptions, cost overruns or associated losses will be avoided.
Substantially all of our revenues are derived from customers located in Maharashtra.

compliance_legal.risk: To obtain a complete understanding of our Company, you should read this section in conjunction with ‘Our Business’ and ‘Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations’ on page 133 and 214 respectively, of this Draft Prospectus as well as the other financial and statistical information contained in this Draft Prospectus.

Accordingly, our business and financial performance are significantly dependent upon the economic conditions, industrial activity, demand environment, regulatory framework and overall business climate prevailing in Maharashtra.
For further details please refer to the chapter titled “Management Discussion and Analysis of Financial Position and Result of Operations” beginning on page 214 of the Draft Prospectus. 5.
Our business is substantially dependent on the experience and expertise of our Promoters, Directors, Key Managerial Personnel and senior management personnel.
Our success is largely attributable to the experience, business relationships and strategic guidance of our Promoters, Mr.
Our Promoters and senior management personnel possess relevant managerial, operational and financial expertise and have developed relationships with customers, suppliers and other stakeholders.
Any inability to retain the services of our Promoters, senior management personnel or other key employees may adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition.

Our business operations are also dependent upon the services of our Directors, Key Managerial Personnel and other senior management personnel, who possess operational, managerial and financial expertise relevant to our business.

The loss of the services of any of our Promoters, Directors, Key Managerial Personnel or senior management personnel due to resignation, retirement, incapacity, death or any other reason, or our inability to attract and retain suitably qualified personnel, may adversely affect our operations, customer and supplier relationships, implementation of business strategies and future growth plans.
For further details please refer to the chapter titled “Our Management” beginning on page 184 of the Draft Prospectus. 11.
The funding requirements for our Objects have not been appraised by any bank or financial institution and are based on our management’s estimates.
The funding requirements for the Objects of the Issue have been determined by our management and have not been appraised by any bank, financial institution or any independent agency.

Accordingly, the estimated costs and deployment of the Net Proceeds are based on certain assumptions and estimates made by our management, which may require revision due to various factors, including changes in business requirements, market conditions, regulatory developments and other unforeseen circumstances.

In the event of any variation in the utilization of the Net Proceeds from the Objects of the Issue, we shall be required to comply with the applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, the SEBI ICDR Regulations and other applicable laws, including obtaining approvals as may be required.
The estimated project cost and implementation schedule have been prepared based on quotations received from vendors, discussions with suppliers and management estimates.

Any delay in acquisition of the office premises, procurement and installation of machinery, commencement of operations, receipt of statutory approvals, availability of contractors or suppliers, or any increase in project costs may adversely affect the implementation schedule.
Our business requires us to obtain, maintain and renew various statutory approvals, registrations, licences and permits.

Any failure to obtain, maintain or renew such approvals in a timely manner, or comply with the conditions applicable thereto, may adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition.
Our business operations require various approvals, registrations, licences and permits from governmental and regulatory authorities.
Such approvals are subject to specified conditions and, in certain cases, require periodic renewals, amendments or fresh applications in the ordinary course of business.

Any failure to obtain, maintain, renew or comply with the conditions applicable to such approvals, registrations, licences or permits may result in regulatory action, including suspension, revocation, cancellation, non-renewal, penalties or restrictions on our operations.
In such circumstances, we may be unable to carry on certain business activities until the relevant approvals are obtained, restored or renewed.
Further, there can be no assurance that approvals, renewals, amendments or fresh applications that may be required in the future will be obtained in a timely manner or at all.

Any delay in obtaining or renewing such approvals, or any failure to comply with applicable regulatory requirements, may disrupt our operations and materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.

financial_valuation.risk: If any one or more of the following risks as well as other risks and uncertainties discussed in this Draft Prospectus were to occur, our business, financial condition and results of our operation could suffer material adverse effects, and could cause the trading price of our Equity Shares and the value of investment in the Equity Shares to materially decline which could result in the loss of all or part of your investment.

Further, any failure to implement the proposed expansion within the estimated budget or timeline may adversely affect our business operations, growth prospects, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.

Any adverse economic, regulatory, political, environmental or business developments in Maharashtra, or our inability to diversify our geographical concentration, could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.

Consequently, our inability to diversify our customer base and operations or mitigate the risks arising from such geographical concentration may have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.

Any inability to successfully implement our growth strategy, including the acquisition and operationalisation of the proposed office premises, may adversely affect our business prospects, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.
The loss of, or reduction in orders from, any significant customer may adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition.

Given the concentration of our revenues among a limited number of significant customers, the loss of one or more such customers, deterioration in their financial condition, inability to maintain satisfactory business relationships with them, or failure to secure repeat or additional orders from existing or new customers may materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.

Accordingly, any adverse developments affecting our key suppliers or our inability to procure raw materials from alternate sources on commercially acceptable terms may materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.

Any damage to, loss of, or deterioration in the quality of our raw materials, work-in-progress or finished goods due to improper storage, handling, processing or other unforeseen events may adversely affect our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.

Any damage to, loss of, theft of, or deterioration in the quality of such inventories arising from improper storage, handling or processing, equipment failure, accidents, fire, natural calamities, water leakage, contamination or other unforeseen events may adversely affect the quality and availability of our inventories.

Any such damage or deterioration may result in loss of inventory, interruption of manufacturing operations, delays in execution of customer orders, increased operating costs, inventory write-offs and reduced revenues.

Although we maintain insurance coverage for our inventories, there can be no assurance that such insurance will be adequate to cover all losses that may arise or that claims made under such policies will be fully recoverable in a timely manner.

internal_operational.risk: We intend to utilise a portion of the Net Proceeds towards the acquisition and installation of plant and machinery for the proposed expansion of our manufacturing facility.

Our Company proposes to utilise ₹285.00 lakhs out of the Net Proceeds of the Issue towards the purchase and installation of additional machinery for the proposed expansion of its manufacturing facility.

Our Company has identified certain plant and machinery proposed to be acquired and installed at its manufacturing facility situated at Gala No. 10, Building No. 3, Jay Chamundeshwari Industrial Complex, Valiv, Vasai East, Maharashtra, India.
The proposed expenditure is based on quotations obtained from Marshal Manufacture and Yadgaar Enterprises.
We have obtained quotations from respective vendors / suppliers and is yet to place any orders or enter into definitive agreements for purchase of plant & machinery.
Accordingly, we cannot assure you that the proposed plant and machinery will be procured at the estimated cost or within the anticipated timelines.
While we may seek to mitigate the impact of unforeseen events, there can be no assurance that all delays, disruptions, cost overruns or associated losses will be avoided.
Substantially all of our revenues are derived from customers located in Maharashtra.
Our business exhibits significant geographical concentration, with substantially all of our revenues being derived from customers located in Maharashtra.

For Fiscal 2026, Fiscal 2025, the period from April 1, 2024 to September 30, 2024 and Fiscal 2024, approximately 99.99%, 99.93%, 97.91% and 98.56%, respectively, of our revenue from operations was generated from customers located in Maharashtra.

Any adverse developments affecting Maharashtra, including economic slowdown, reduction in industrial activity, changes in governmental policies or regulations, labour disruptions, infrastructure constraints, natural calamities, public health emergencies, supply chain disruptions or other region-specific events, may adversely affect our customers and their demand for our products, which could in turn adversely affect our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.
Further, our manufacturing facility situated at Vasai, Palghar, Maharashtra and our warehouse located at Palghar, Maharashtra are also situated within the same state.

Any disruption affecting Maharashtra, including disruptions in transportation networks, utilities, logistics infrastructure, labour availability, regulatory approvals or other operational factors, could adversely affect our manufacturing, warehousing and distribution activities and consequently have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.
While we may seek to expand our customer base and geographical presence over time, there can be no assurance that we will be successful in reducing our geographical concentration.

Any inability to diversify our customer base across other regions may continue to expose us to concentration risks and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and future prospects.

Any economic slowdown, decline in industrial or manufacturing activity, reduction in customer demand, changes in governmental policies, taxation or regulatory framework, or deterioration in the overall business environment in Maharashtra may adversely affect demand for our products, including wire products, fasteners and allied products, thereby adversely affecting our revenues, profitability and cash flows.

Further, any disruption affecting Maharashtra, including disruptions in transportation networks, logistics infrastructure, utilities, labour availability, natural calamities, public health emergencies, civil disturbances or other unforeseen events, may adversely affect our ability to procure raw materials, manufacture products, deliver products to customers and maintain continuity of operations.

Such disruptions may result in delays in execution of customer orders, increased operating costs, loss of business opportunities and reduced profitability, which could materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition.

Additionally, the concentration of our customer base in Maharashtra limits our ability to offset adverse developments in such region through revenues generated from customers located in other geographies.

Since substantially all of our revenues are derived from customers located in Maharashtra, any adverse developments affecting the region could have a disproportionate impact on our business and financial performance.
Further, increased competition, pricing pressures, changing customer requirements or the loss of significant customers in the region may adversely affect our market position and profitability.
Our manufacturing facility and warehouse are also located in Maharashtra, which further increases our exposure to region-specific risks.

Our customers may reduce the volume of orders placed with us due to various factors beyond our control, including changes in their procurement policies, financial condition, business strategies, product requirements, inventory management practices, demand patterns, increased competition, preference for alternative suppliers or adverse conditions affecting their industries.

As we generally operate without long-term contractual commitments from our customers, our ability to forecast demand, plan production schedules, manage inventory levels, procure raw materials and efficiently utilise our manufacturing capacity may be adversely affected.

Any delay, postponement, cancellation or reduction in purchase orders from our existing customers, or our inability to replace lost business with new customers on commercially acceptable terms, may result in underutilisation of capacity, lower revenues, increased operating costs and reduced profitability.
A substantial portion of our raw material purchases is dependent upon a limited number of suppliers.

Any interruption in the supply of raw materials or our inability to procure raw materials from such suppliers on commercially acceptable terms may adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition.
Our business is dependent on the timely and adequate availability of raw materials required for the manufacturing and trading of wire and wire products and fasteners.
We procure a substantial portion of our raw material requirements from a limited number of suppliers.

Our top one supplier accounted for 17.54%, 24.42%, 44.18% and 60.89% of our total purchases for Fiscal 2026, Fiscal 2025, the period from April 1, 2024 to September 30, 2024 and Fiscal 2024, respectively.
Further, our top three suppliers contributed 45.33%, 49.68%, 81.87% and 81.97%, respectively, of our total purchases during such periods.

Our top five suppliers accounted for 61.21%, 66.57%, 100.00% and 87.71%, respectively, of our purchases, while our top ten suppliers contributed 84.42%, 84.11% and 93.27%, respectively, of our purchases during the aforesaid periods. (In lakhs) Pursuant to the certificate dated, June 06, 2026 from our Statutory Auditor M/s Bohara Shah & Co, Chartered Accountants.

Our dependence on a limited number of suppliers exposes us to risks associated with disruption in supply, reduction in credit periods, inability to procure raw materials in required quantities, increase in prices, deterioration in quality standards, changes in commercial terms or discontinuation of business relationships.
Further, we generally do not have long-term supply agreements with our suppliers and procure raw materials based on purchase orders and prevailing market conditions.

Any delay or interruption in the availability of raw materials due to capacity constraints, operational issues, financial difficulties, insolvency, labour unrest, transportation disruptions, regulatory changes, geopolitical developments, natural calamities, pandemics or other unforeseen events affecting our suppliers may adversely affect our manufacturing schedules and ability to fulfil customer orders in a timely manner.
Such circumstances may result in increased procurement costs, disruptions in operations, delays in execution of orders, lower margins and loss of customers.

strategy_growth.risk: The prices of such raw materials are subject to fluctuations arising from factors beyond our control, including changes in steel and metal prices, domestic and global demand and supply conditions, inflation, transportation costs, foreign exchange movements, government policies and other market conditions.

Such competitors may be able to offer products at more competitive prices, undertake more aggressive marketing initiatives, invest in capacity expansion, technology upgrades and research and development activities, or absorb adverse market conditions more effectively than us.

The prices of steel wire, wire rods and other raw materials used in our manufacturing process may fluctuate due to changes in market demand, supply disruptions, inflationary pressures, changes in government policies, import- export regulations, geopolitical events or other factors beyond our control.

Gold prices are highly volatile and are influenced by various factors beyond our control, including global demand and supply dynamics, inflation, interest rates, geopolitical developments, currency exchange rate fluctuations, governmental policies, changes in import duties and other macroeconomic factors.

In addition, an increase in India’s trade deficit, a downgrading in India’s sovereign debt rating or a decline in India’s foreign exchange reserves could increase interest rates and adversely affect liquidity, which could adversely affect the Indian economy and our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition. 34.
Our international operations are subject to many uncertainties and we are exposed to foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations.

We may be subject to risks inherently associated with international operations, including risks associated with foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations, which may cause volatility in our reported income, and risks associated with the application and imposition of protective legislation and regulations relating to import or export or otherwise resulting from foreign policy or the variability of foreign economic conditions. 43.

The rate of economic liberalization could change, and specific laws and policies affecting companies in the industrial equipment manufacturing sectors, foreign investment, currency exchange rates and other matters affecting investment in our securities could change as well.
Any dividends in respect of our Equity Shares will also be paid in Indian Rupees and subsequently converted into the relevant foreign currency for repatriation, if required.
Any adverse movement in currency exchange rates during the time taken for such conversion may reduce the net dividend to foreign investors.

In addition, any adverse movement in currencyexchange rates during a delay in repatriating the proceeds from a sale of Equity Shares outside India, for example, because of a delay in regulatory approvals that may be required for the sale of Equity Shares may reduce the proceeds received by Shareholders.

Under the foreign exchange regulations currently in force in India, transfers of shares between non-residents and residents are freely permitted (subject to certain exceptions) if they comply with the pricing guidelines and reporting requirements specified by the RBI.

Additionally, shareholders who seek to convert the Rupee proceeds from a sale of shares in India into foreign currency and repatriate that foreign currency from India will require a no objection/ tax clearance certificate from the income tax authority.
